notesStmt.note: These lines bear only slight resemblance to the final published poem, suggesting that they constitute an early draft, likely written in 1884 or the first half of 1885.

This manuscript contain early-stage draft lines for "By That Long Scan of Waves," first published along with seven other poems in The Nineteenth Century (August 1885) under the general title "Fancies at Navesink." The poem was later included in November Boughs (1888).

lg.l: How strange the select scenes scenes ye big, capricious gurgles!

How curiously the long the past the war, the sick, and dead,
on the battle-field, itself themselves recalling,
